stack.frontend: HTMX + Tailwind v4 (committed app.css) + a native <details> element — no new JS
stack.deployment: native binary + systemd on the Pi (unchanged)

implementation_notes: The whole feature is two pure functions plus a template rewrite. dashboardLinkState(probes, wan) collapses the probe fleet into one word; primaryNetwork(ifaces) picks the busiest real interface. No new field in DashboardData, no new SSE event, no new query, no goroutine, no database access — every input already reached the partial.

Thresholds are NOT redefined: the verdict reads the same latencyCritLossPct/latencyCritRTTMs constants the sparklines colour by (helpers_sparkline.go). Two threshold sets on one page would eventually contradict each other, and a tile saying 'Stable' above a chart rendered red is worse than either threshold being slightly off.

ADR-2 (the one that matters): 'Unstable' trips at >=10% loss, NOT at >0%. The probe's loss window is 20 samples, so ONE dropped ping is 5%. A >0% rule would flip the tile yellow on a single lost packet on a healthy home link — the tile would cry wolf, the admin would learn to ignore it, and the feature would be worse than the byte counter it replaced. TC-NT-085Bh locks this in.

ADR-3: the subtitle names the BUSIEST interface, never a sum. tailscale0 tunnels over eth0 — summing them double-counts the same bytes the moment the VPN carries traffic, inflating the headline precisely when the admin is looking at it. TC-NT-086f asserts no summed total appears anywhere in the tile.

Rule ORDER carries meaning: WAN down or gateway-not-ok => 'Offline'; a lossy off-box target => 'Unstable'. A box that cannot reach its own gateway has a broken LAN, which is a different problem (and a different fix) from a lossy internet path. Blurring them into one word would make the tile useless exactly when it matters.

The template funcs are registered in BOTH FuncMaps in templates.go (the file carries two — page cache and SSE cache). Registering in one fails silently in the other path, which is why TC-NT-E2E-002h renders through the SSE path specifically.

technical_debt.substitution: dashboardLinkState identifies the gateway probe by matching the label 'gateway'. An operator who renames that target via ULTRON_NET_TARGETS would leave the verdict with no gateway clause: a broken LAN would then read 'Unstable' instead of 'Offline'.
technical_debt.reason: gatewayprobe.Snapshot does not carry the probe's configured Host, so the gateway cannot currently be identified structurally (Host == "") from the snapshot alone. Name-matching is what caused BG-074; this is the same class of weakness, contained.
technical_debt.remediation: Carry the configured Host (or an IsGateway flag) through to gatewayprobe.Snapshot and identify the gateway structurally. That belongs in gatewayprobe, not in the tile. The degradation until then is graceful: the tile still warns, just with a less precise word.

technical_debt.substitution: FR-086 (throughput subtitle + collapsed per-interface disclosure) was retired on 2026-07-14, commit 1a298e6, and its 8 declared test cases removed from 03_TEST_CASES.json. None of those Go functions had ever been written — the spec declared tests for behaviour the owner had already deleted.
technical_debt.reason: Writing them would have re-introduced a product behaviour the owner cut deliberately. NFR-089b was re-scoped at the same time: its BG-072 half guarded a virtual-interface filter that went with FR-086, leaving only the BG-073 label-keyed history to protect.
